title: The handler asks the cache
label: GET
caption: getUser(42) checks UserCache before touching the database.

title: Miss: load from Postgres
label: MISS
caption: user:42 is not cached, so the cache loads it from the source. The handler waits on this read.

title: The cache stores the row
label: FILL
caption: Two of three slots were taken, so user:42 joins as the newest entry and nothing is evicted.

title: The handler gets the value
label: SERVE
caption: The first read paid the database round trip; the next read of user:42 will not.

title: The handler asks for user:7
label: GET
caption: The cache is full and already holds user:7.

title: Hit: Postgres is not called
label: HIT
caption: The value comes from memory. The read also counts as a use, which matters for eviction.

title: Served, and user:7 is the newest
label: SERVE
caption: user:7 moves to the newest end, so user:3 is now the next to be evicted.

title: The handler asks for user:51
label: GET
caption: All three slots are taken; user:7 is the least recently used.

title: Miss on a full cache
label: MISS
caption: The cache loads user:51 and picks the oldest entry, user:7, to make room.

title: user:7 leaves, user:51 enters
label: EVICT
caption: The cache never grows past its capacity: one entry out for each new one in.

title: The handler gets user:51
label: SERVE
caption: A later read of user:7 is a miss again and pays the database round trip.
